name: Claridge's
positioning: Claridge's: a hotel in the heart of Mayfair founded in 1812, with an Art Deco lobby, rooms and suites in Victorian, Art Deco and contemporary styles, and a subterranean spa designed by Andre Fu
best_for: Travelers who want a base in the heart of Mayfair
Guests who want a spa with a pool under a vaulted ceiling

facts.text: Claridge's is in the heart of Mayfair, London.
Mayfair is a quiet neighbourhood of Georgian townhouses, refined restaurants and Savile Row shops.
The suites feature balconies overlooking Brook Street.
The Georgian suite has a Steinberg baby grand piano, a fully equipped kitchen and a 24-hour butler.
Rooms have Dyson Supersonic hairdryers and free Wi-Fi.
The spa has a sauna, steam rooms and a spacious fitness centre.
Afternoon tea includes bespoke Claridge's blends prepared by Henrietta Lovell of the Rare Tea Company.
The Fumoir is a cosy, darkwood 1930s-style bar serving vintage signature cocktails.
Claridge's has a shop of homeware, including an in-house range and pieces made for Claridge's by designers and artisans.
There is elevator access to all floors, and the restaurant, bar and reception areas are flat.

highlights.text: The lobby, with its chequered floor, captures the Art Deco glamour of the Jazz Age.
The subterranean spa was designed by Andre Fu, with limewood and stone textures.
The spa's swimming pool sits beneath a vaulted ceiling, surrounded by stone columns and cabanas.
The suites and rooms span Victorian opulence, Art Deco glamour and contemporary elegance.
The ArtSpace Cafe, designed by John Pawson, has its own entrance on Brook's Mews and a gallery of rotating exhibitions.

considerations.text: Mayfair is quiet rather than cool and trendy.
WhataHotel notes a formal atmosphere that may not suit all travelers.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting its ultra-luxury positioning.
